overall_notes: Round 2 retrofit clears the strict bar with all six categories at Level 4. ALIGNMENT: D2.2 'make and test predictions about mean and mode across populations' is faithfully addressed; expanded_walkthrough cross-references Lesson 3 ('Yesterday Lesson 3 compared two populations') and Lesson 5 ('Lesson 5 capstones'). PEDAGOGICAL_DEPTH: trap names Konold (1989) outcome approach AND Konold & Pollatsek (2002) signal-vs-noise; recovery_moves branch by three diagnostics (A: 'same kind of data' shortcut, B: ignores mode, C: cannot articulate comparison) — sub-level teacher-actionable. INSTRUCTIONAL_BALANCE: puppets explicitly OPTIONAL with stuffed-animal/paper-bag/picture substitutions; NO-PREP teacher-read version embedded in differentiation ('teacher reads two short data sets aloud (Class A: 2,4,6,4; Class B: 4,4,5,3); children chant the mean and mode aloud'); 12/25/13 = 50 min sits cleanly in the G3 45-50 band. CLARITY_VOICE: Maybe Mae anchors hook, action, consolidation, and exit_routine; 'PREDICT, then TEST, then TELL!' is the quotable refrain repeated in hook and 3x at exit; every success criterion is first-person 'I can'. MATHEMATICAL_AUTHENTICITY: action step 6 introduces a STRATEGY COMPARE — some pairs add-then-divide, some estimate, class compares accuracy with Konold reminder that predictions must be TESTED; mean as 'fair share' / mode as 'most common' defined precisely in blueprint and reinforced. LESSON_WORKSHEET_CONSISTENCY: worksheet_title 'Maybe Mae's Mean and Mode' matches lesson.worksheet_brief.worksheet_title verbatim; Part 1 practises SC#3 (predict), Part 2 practises SC#1+SC#2 (compute mean and mode), Part 3 practises SC#4 (test/explain) with a sentence-frame transfer format that varies from the raw compute drill in the action — justified verification of generalisation.
